topics.title: The keyv npm Worm: How 444 Packages and 2 Billion Installs Got Poisoned With Valid Provenance
topics.whyTrending: August 4, 2026 - attackers took over the maintainer account behind keyv (127M weekly downloads), flat-cache (565M/mo), file-entry-cache (557M/mo) and cacheable, pushed straight to main and cut releases. 444 packages across 1381 versions shipped a preinstall hook that downloaded Bun and ran a 728KB obfuscated stealer targeting .npmrc tokens, gh CLI tokens, AWS creds, Vault tokens and kubeconfigs. The nasty part: every poisoned version had valid GitHub Actions provenance. Self-propagating (tracked as keyv-shai-hulud). Eight days old, no calm engineering postmortem written yet.

topics.title: Kill Install Scripts: A Post-keyv Hardening Playbook for npm, pnpm and CI
topics.whyTrending: Direct practical follow-up to the keyv worm - the attack only worked because preinstall runs by default. Concrete controls exist and almost nobody has them on: ignore-scripts, pnpm onlyBuiltDependencies allowlists, minimumReleaseAge cooldowns, lockfile pinning, npm audit signatures, isolated CI runners with scoped tokens. Turns a scary headline into a checklist a team can ship in an afternoon.

topics.title: Claude Code on Your Own Metal: Self-Hosted Runners, and What Still Leaves Your Network
topics.whyTrending: Public beta opened August 6, 2026 (6 days ago) for Team and Enterprise. One command, `claude self-hosted-runner`, moves cloud session execution onto your own machines - repo checkouts, build artifacts and secrets stay put. But prompts, model responses, tool results and transcripts still travel to Anthropic for inference, and it is unavailable under ZDR. That gap is exactly what security reviewers will ask about and what nobody is writing honestly about yet.

topics.title: Vite 8 + Rolldown: The Migration That Cut Linear's Build From 46s to 6s
topics.whyTrending: Vite 8 shipped stable March 12, 2026 with Rolldown (Rust) replacing both esbuild and Rollup, now several patches in (8.1.3, July 2). Official benchmark: 19k modules in 1.61s vs Rollup's 40.10s. The compat layer handles most config, so the real story is the failure mode - plugins that reach into Rollup or esbuild internals. A migration war-story with actual numbers, not another release summary.

topics.title: MCP Apps Are Final: Shipping Interactive HTML UIs From Your MCP Server
topics.whyTrending: MCP Apps became the first official MCP extension (Final Jan 26, 2026) and its spec was republished with the 2026-07-28 release. Servers now declare ui:// resources, hosts render them in a sandboxed iframe, and UI-to-host talk is JSON-RPC over postMessage routed through the normal consent path. Claude web/desktop, Goose, VS Code Insiders and ChatGPT all render it. Natural sequel to the stateless-spec post and a genuinely buildable tutorial.

topics.title: TypeScript 7 One Month After GA: Real Migration Numbers, Real Blockers
topics.whyTrending: GA landed July 8, 2026 - the Go-native compiler, 8-12x faster on full builds. A month in there is finally field data instead of RC speculation: which ESLint type-aware setups break, what tsc plugins have no path forward, how the language service behaves in monorepos. Follows up on our pre-GA readiness post with what actually happened.

topics.title: Agent Observability: Silent Watchdogs, Infinite Retries and Phantom Events in Production
topics.whyTrending: The failure modes of production agents are finally being written down - stranded tickets, retry storms, events that fire for work that never happened, watchdogs that die quietly. This is the operational layer nobody covers: what to trace, what to alert on, what a good agent SLO looks like. Pairs with OpenTelemetry tooling we've already covered.

topics.title: Oxlint Is 110x Faster Than ESLint - And Still Can't Replace It. Here's the Hybrid Setup
topics.whyTrending: 650+ rules in Rust, Mercedes-Benz reports 71% less lint time, JS plugins alpha landed March 2026. But downloads tell the truth: ESLint 68M/week vs Oxlint 638K, because eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y, next/core-web-vitals and custom rules have no equivalent. The honest answer is running both - fast pass in the editor and pre-commit, type-aware ESLint in CI. Contrarian, practical, benchmarkable.

topics.title: Agent Cost Governance: Gateway Spending Limits, Token Budgets and Who Pays for the Runaway Loop
topics.whyTrending: Claude Code v2.1.225 (Aug 7, 2026) started enforcing gateway spending limits with explicit notifications, and billing attribution is being reworked across agent tools including Devin. Teams running fleets of background agents now need real budget architecture: per-repo caps, model tiering, attribution to teams, and alerting before the invoice. Underserved topic with a fresh hook.

topics.title: React Under the Linux Foundation: What Actually Changed for Your Codebase
topics.whyTrending: React moved to an independent React Foundation under the Linux Foundation, and the 19.x line keeps shipping patches (19.2.7, June 2026) with no React 20 in sight despite the clickbait. Worth a grounded piece on what neutral governance means for RSC direction, the Compiler's roadmap and framework lock-in risk - the strategic read most posts skip in favor of feature lists.
